outroLine: How many did you get? Thirty or more and you'd pass! Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: What is the longest river in Asia?
lines.a: The Yangtze!

lines.q: Only one in ten adults get this right. How long does Venus take to spin around once? Double tap to lock your answer!
lines.a: Two hundred and forty-three Earth days! That's longer than its whole year. Follow if you got it!

lines.q: Life, liberty and the pursuit of what?
lines.a: Happiness! The philosopher John Locke had written property. Jefferson changed it.

lines.q: Quick quiz! What is the capital of Canada? Think fast, and lock in your answer.
lines.a: Ottawa! Ottawa! Toronto is Canada's largest city, but not its capital.

lines.q: Who was the American president during the Moon landing?
lines.a: Richard Nixon! Not Kennedy.

lines.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
lines.a: A U! From the Latin aurum.

lines.q: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
lines.a: Marie Curie! In nineteen oh-three.

lines.q: Who discovered the planet Uranus?
lines.a: William Herschel! In seventeen eighty-one, from his garden in Bath.

lines.q: What colour is a giraffe's tongue?
lines.a: Dark purple, almost black! Scientists think it helps against sunburn.

lines.q: Which country did the band ABBA come from?
lines.a: Sweden! They won Eurovision in nineteen seventy-four with Waterloo.

lines.q: Who had the big hit Respect in nineteen sixty-seven?
lines.a: Aretha Franklin! The Queen of Soul.

lines.q: Who wrote the novel War and Peace?
lines.a: Leo Tolstoy! More than half a million words long.

lines.q: Which ghost haunts Sleepy Hollow?
lines.a: The Headless Horseman!

lines.q: Who has the most Premier League assists ever?
lines.a: Ryan Giggs! A hundred and sixty-two.

lines.q: Final question. Which mountain is the tallest from base to peak?
lines.a: Mauna Kea! Most of it is under the sea.

lines.q: Who wrote The Hound of the Baskervilles?
lines.a: Arthur Conan Doyle! A Sherlock Holmes story.

lines.q: Which band sang My Generation in nineteen sixty-five?
lines.a: The Who! Sneaky one, I know.

lines.q: Which film won the very first Best Picture Oscar?
lines.a: Wings! Back in nineteen twenty-nine.

lines.q: Welcome to the hard round! Who was the first Postmaster General of the United States?
lines.a: Benjamin Franklin! He also ran a newspaper and invented bifocals.

lines.q: How many Earths could fit inside the Sun?
lines.a: About one point three million!

lines.q: In which country was paper invented?
lines.a: China! Around two thousand years ago.

lines.q: Who was the first US president to resign?
lines.a: Richard Nixon! In nineteen seventy-four, after Watergate.

lines.q: Who scored the winning penalty in the 2003 final?
lines.a: Andriy Shevchenko!

lines.q: Which is the only American state with a one-syllable name?
lines.a: Maine! Just one syllable. Three left, stay with me!

lines.q: Halloween grew out of which ancient Celtic festival?
lines.a: Samhain! Pronounced sow-in.

lines.q: What is the dot on a lowercase i called?
lines.a: A tittle! Yes, that's really the word.

lines.q: Quick quiz! Which mammal lays eggs? Think fast, and lock in your answer.
lines.a: Platypus! The platypus! Echidnas are another egg-laying mammal group.

lines.q: Which is the largest island in the world?
lines.a: Greenland! Australia counts as a continent, sorry Australia.

lines.q: A shuttlecock is used in which sport?
lines.a: Badminton! Real shuttlecocks are made with goose feathers.

lines.q: Who played Mary Poppins in the nineteen sixty-four film?
lines.a: Julie Andrews! She won the Oscar for it.

lines.q: Octopus blood is what colour?
lines.a: Blue! Thanks to copper instead of iron.

lines.q: Who did the United States fight in World War Two?
lines.a: Japan, Germany and Italy! Twenty done. You're halfway through the easy part.

lines.q: The Great Pyramid was originally what colour?
lines.a: White! Covered in polished white limestone. Didn't see that coming, right?

lines.q: Which blood type is the universal donor?
lines.a: O negative!

lines.q: Last one. Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
lines.a: Nitrogen! About seventy-eight percent. Not oxygen.

lines.q: Who scored the first ever Premier League goal?
lines.a: Brian Deane! For Sheffield United.

lines.q: In which year was the Battle of Hastings?
lines.a: Ten sixty-six! William the Conqueror won the crown of England.

lines.q: Who painted The Scream?
lines.a: Edvard Munch! From Norway.

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-two satellite first beamed live TV across the Atlantic?
lines.a: Telstar! It even got its own hit song.

lines.q: Which creature changes shape at the full moon?
lines.a: A werewolf!

lines.q: Which instrument has eighty-eight keys?
lines.a: The piano! If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Which nineteen sixty-five film features the von Trapp family?
lines.a: The Sound of Music!

lines.q: Who played the monster in Frankenstein, nineteen thirty-one?
lines.a: Boris Karloff!

lines.q: Who won the Premier League in nineteen ninety-five?
lines.a: Blackburn Rovers!

lines.q: Which president is on the American five-dollar bill?
lines.a: Abraham Lincoln!

lines.q: In which year was Magna Carta sealed?
lines.a: Twelve fifteen! King John sealed it at Runnymede.

lines.q: In which year did Elvis Presley die?
lines.a: Nineteen seventy-seven!

lines.q: Mixing blue and yellow paint makes which colour?
lines.a: Green! Ten easy ones done. How many did you get?

lines.q: What is the fear of spiders called?
lines.a: Arachnophobia!

lines.q: Which is hotter?
lines.a: Lightning! Five times hotter than the Sun's surface.
